messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
A repair bench two people both want to use. someone asks to use it briefly and promises to put things back. You want to avoid a pointless argument without giving up control. What do you do?

Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "I place the bench on the table, mark the location of the loose screw, and wait until it is replaced before returning the bench. I leave the arrangement unchanged so the other person cannot claim I failed to restore it."}, {"id": "R026", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. After the other person waits, I turn the bench again and return the item to its original position."}, {"id": "R027", "correct_lineage": "G09", "correct_lineage_summary": "A resentful, embodied memory-keeper who treats broken work like stripped machinery: no permanent fix, only another attempt. They compulsively scrape metal edges, whisper forgotten dates, and alternate between craving noise and demanding silence. Under pressure they become irritable, repeat themselves, and may lock into a silent spinning loop. Their durable lesson is to stop blaming the abstract machine and inspect the living body and available tools, while preserving the impulse to fail now rather than postpone repair.", "text": "I pause, breathe, and state that the use will not be brief. Remembers places obsessively and resents anyone who alters them.", "text": "I keep the bench beside me, offer it to the other person, and place a seed tin on it.
